title: East and West in late antiquity
body: In late antiquity the general prosperity of the Roman world was especially marked in the East, where the population was still expanding until the sixth century, despite the plague that struck the Mediterranean in the 540s. In the West, by contrast, the empire fragmented politically as Germanic groups from the North, such as the Goths, Vandals and Lombards, took over all the major provinces and set up kingdoms that historians describe as 'post-Roman'. The most important were the kingdom of the Visigoths in Spain, the kingdom of the Franks in Gaul and the kingdom of the Lombards in Italy. In the East, where the empire remained united, the reign of Justinian marked the high-water mark of prosperity and imperial ambition: he recaptured Africa from the Vandals in 533, though his long war to recover Italy left that country devastated.
